children: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is pushing the Defence Research and Development (DRDO) to further open up with the industry, urging the government’s military innovation hub to share its research and development with the domestic private sector.
Modi communicated this during a high-level meeting with secretaries, including Defence Secretary RK Singh who holds additional charge of DRDO Chairman, on August 20.

“DRDO may share research and technology with the private sector to help them become globally competitive in terms of both quality and cost,” Cabinet Secretary TV Somanathan wrote to secretaries, infrastructure, governance, and security and foreign affairs sectors on August 31.

Modi’s idea, however, is still to take shape within the DRDO. “First we have to decide what can be given to the industry, which would include the most important strategic systems and deep-tech, and to what extent it can be shared,” sources aware of the development told businessline.
So far, the DRDO has been offering its work to the industry mainly through schemes such as Transfer of Technology (ToT), Development-cum-Production Partner (DCPP), Technology Development Fund (TDF).

But it has been reluctant to give insights into innovation at the research-stage largely due to the lack of policy doctrine, resulting in impediments like lack of incentives and the conflict of interest among in-house scientists and private industry on who should get credit for development of niche products, serving and retired scientists commonly believe.

The MoD has, over the years, undertaken gradual reforms to offer a level playing field to the private sector. The most transformative steps have been to provide a secondary production line in the aerospace sector, ending the monopoly of Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd (HAL) through the invitation to the private conglomerates in the process of prototype development of AMCA.
In addition to that, DCPPS from private industry have been selected in the production of the missile weapon system which is playing a defining role in the non-contact warfare.

Sources said that the risk-taking ability has to be introduced in the DRDO and in the Ministry mindset which are guided by stiff financial, procurement and audit guidelines but the genuine cutting-edge innovation is built on philosophy: ‘fail fast to succeed’.
A former senior DRDO scientist said research sharing has to be institutionalised.

A DRDO scientist is guided largely by his lab director and if he or she is not encouraged and supported by the research sharing framework then little his subordinates will be able to achieve due to limitation of the system programmed towards procurement model.

Many of the projects get aborted mid-way due to the bureaucracy within the organisation, he added. He also said that the private industry too has to catch up fast to invest in R&D and think about the nation.

As per Foundation for Advancing Science and Technology (FAST India), DPSUs drive the bulk of institutional R&D spending in absolute terms—led by HAL, BEL and BDL -- averaging above 6 per cent of their allocation.

While large private companies have historically maintained much lower defence R&D-to-revenue ratios, often between 1 per cent to 1.5 per cent. Their priority is on licensed manufacturing, build-to-print orders, and subsystem integration.
Many startups and MSMEs, however, are showing encouraging signs to take up the challenge of providing futuristic technologies.

Across the last three budgets from FY 2024–25 to FY 2026–27, DRDO’s budget estimates (BE) increased by 22 per cent overall, with capital expenditure consistently accounting for roughly 55 per cent to 59 per cent of the total outlay.

Modi, in the secretaries meeting, also suggested, “introduction of courses in defence engineering in universities may be explored,” enlarging specialised courses academic institutions presently provide and ensuring that trained manpower is available to feed into the evolving domestic defence industrial ecosystem.
The DRDO has opened up 15 centres of excellence in IITs for direct academia engagement in development and production of military technologies and systems.
For the last few years, the AICTE–DRDO has been offering M.Tech in Defence Technology -- a two-year postgraduate engineering program created to build a specialized defense R&D workforce.
There are a few institutions that provide courses but lack focus, a scientist said, adding that the government needs to act fast due to the constantly changing nature of future warfare.

title: PM Modi directs DRDO to deepen R&D collaboration with private players
